declared: 2026-11-28, before any factorial run (Phase 3 of the flask_v2 plan). Inputs: results/diagnostics/v2_mechanism/RESULT.md (L1, L3, L5 carried) and results/diagnostics/propagation_dynoplan_v10 (L6, declared 2026-11-25 as a labelled variant; source = the baseline library's own defaults, Dynoplan benchmark/config/algs/sst_v0.yaml, unicycle control duration 2-20 x 0.1 s). A quick smoke run on dev seeds 1001-1010 (parallel, untimed) preceded this file; it informed which levers act on which planner, not the rule below.
timing: serial, process pinned to config/machine.json measurement_cpu (10), sibling idle; plan_ns + postprocess_ns

grid.unicycle sst_bvp, sst_simd, rrt_dp: L3 x L5 x L6 (8 configurations each)

rule: 1. Per (case, algorithm), a configuration is eligible only if every one of the 10 attempts returns a path valid on the ORIGINAL model (planning.validate dense check; the interval certificate of order-4 paths runs in the held-out campaign, as in v10b). Otherwise maximise the valid count first.
2. Among eligible configurations pick the lowest MEAN planning time (plan + post-processing), because the paper's Table I reports means.
3. Simplicity tie-break: a configuration with fewer levers switched on replaces the winner when its mean is within 10 % of the winner's.

4. One configuration per (robot family, algorithm) is frozen for the held-out campaign: the configuration chosen for the most cases of that family/algorithm; ties resolved by the lower summed mean time over the family's cases. (A single setting per planner, not per environment, as the paper uses one planner per row.)
5. Never select by closeness to the paper's numbers. Path length is reported, not optimised.
